name: University of Chichester

settingEvidence.evidence: Our Bishop Otter campus in Chichester is set in beautiful surroundings with plenty of relaxing green space and a combination of attractive, historic buildings and excellent modern facilities.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students starting in 2027 (2027/28), as shown on the Accounting and Finance, Business Management and Fintech course pages. Other course pages still show the 2026/27 fee of £9,790 ('Subject to Parliamentary approval').

livingCosts.text: University halls at the Chichester (Bishop Otter) campus and nearby city properties cost about £180–£228 a week (2026/27); the cheapest are the 50-week city-centre houses and the dearest the 39-week on-campus halls. Some halls are catered, some self-catered. Wifi is included in the rent.

source.evidence: Prices listed are for the 2026/27 academic year.

contextual.summary: UK applicants whose circumstances match Chichester's contextual factors may get an offer 16 UCAS tariff points lower (about two A-level grades); there is no separate form, you apply through UCAS as normal.
contextual.typicalReduction: 16 UCAS tariff points (equivalent to two A-level grades or one BTEC grade); 8 points for foundation year courses

criteria.detail: Having been in receipt of free school meals during your secondary education.
Living within POLAR4 quintile 1 (postcode areas with the lowest rates of participation in higher education).
Being a care leaver: having been in formal care for at least three months.
Having caring responsibilities: being an unpaid carer for a family member or a friend.
You or a parent/carer currently serve, or have served, in the UK Armed Forces.

Having declared a disability: a social or communication condition such as autism; blindness or serious visual impairment uncorrected by glasses; deafness or serious hearing impediment; a long-term or chronic health condition such as diabetes, epilepsy or cancer; a mental health condition such as depression, schizophrenia or anxiety disorder; or a physical impairment or mobility issues.

contextual.rulesText: Open to UK applicants applying for undergraduate courses. The page says these factors 'are considered when deciding if you are eligible' and does not say how many you need. Apply through UCAS as normal; Chichester may ask for evidence. If you are predicted two or more A-level grades better than the published typical offer you will normally be made the typical offer. Some courses with course-specific entry requirements may differ.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is an entry requirement reduction of 16 UCAS tariff points (equivalent to two A-level grades or one BTEC grade) for all eligible undergraduate degree courses.

notes: Chichester doesn't appear to offer a standalone Economics degree: none is listed on its Business School or undergraduate course pages (checked 2026-10-21). The courses recorded are the closest matches (accounting and finance, fintech, business management).
Offers are in UCAS tariff points: 104 points (BCC at A level) for most courses; Fintech 104-120 points (BCC to BBB). The pages say individual offers may vary.

Business Management and Finance and Business Management and Marketing still show 2026/27 details (2026 entry) on 2026-10-21; Accounting and Finance, Business Management and Fintech show 2027/28 fees (2027 entry).

No admissions test is named on any course page, and Chichester is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry (https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/01172717/Course_List_2027_Entry_Final.pdf).

Chichester's Outreach team offers talks, workshops and academic taster sessions (many for Year 12+, including Business School sessions) on request for schools and colleges; no application programme or summer school for individual students was found.
Business School courses are taught at the Bishop Otter campus in Chichester; the university's other campus is at Bognor Regis.
The accommodation page's detailed hall descriptions show older, lower prices than its 2026/27 comparison table; the table (which states 2026/27) was used.
Chichester's Halls vs Home page says all utility bills are included in the rent for university halls (https://www.chi.ac.uk/halls-vs-home/).
